sentences.zh: 来自萨夫什金娜街55号。

sentences.en: He had been monitoring all of the content posted from 55 Savushkina for weeks and had assembled a huge database of troll content.
sentences.zh: 他已经连续几周监控从萨夫什金娜街55号发布的所有内容，并收集了巨大的水军内容数据库。

sentences.en: He brought up InfoSurfing's YouTube channel, and as we scrolled down, I noticed several videos in the same style as the Secret Service animation.
sentences.zh: 他调出了InfoSurfing的YouTube频道，当我们向下滚动时，我注意到了几个与特勤局动画风格相同的视频。

sentences.en: In fact, InfoSurfing had posted the exact same video on its own account, except instead of the unfortunate Australian voiceover, it was narrated in Russian.
sentences.zh: 事实上，InfoSurfing在其自己的账号上发布了完全相同的视频，只是配音不是倒霉的澳大利亚口音，而是用俄语叙述的。

sentences.en: It was the most tantalizing connection yet.
sentences.zh: 这是迄今为止最诱人的联系。

sentences.en: It seemed as if the man in the hoax videos had worked for an outfit connected to the same building that housed the Internet Research Agency.
sentences.zh: 造假视频中的那个男人似乎曾在与互联网研究局位于同一栋建筑内的机构工作过。

sentences.en: Still, no one had heard of any department that might have orchestrated the hoax.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，没有人听说过任何可能策划了这场造假骗局的部门。

sentences.en: The English language trolling team was an elite and secretive group.
sentences.zh: 英语水军团队是一个精英且秘密的群体。

sentences.en: Marat Burkhardt, who worked in the forums department, was asked to try out for an English language team, but didn't get the job.
sentences.zh: 在论坛部门工作的马拉特·布尔哈特被要求参加英语团队的选拔，但没有得到这份工作。

sentences.en: The only person I spoke with who worked in the English department was a woman named Katarina Aistova.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的唯一在英语部门工作过的人是一个名叫卡塔琳娜·艾斯托娃的女人。

sentences.en: A former hotel receptionist, she told me she joined the Internet Research Agency when it was in a previous smaller office.
sentences.zh: 她曾是一名酒店前台，她告诉我当互联网研究局还设在一个较小的旧办公室时她就加入了。

sentences.en: I found her through the Anonymous International leak, which included emails she had sent to her bosses reporting on the
sentences.zh: 我是通过“国际匿名者”的泄密事件找到她的，其中包含了她发送给老板们的电子邮件，汇报了她在

sentences.en: pro-Putin comments she left on sites like The Blaze and Politico.
sentences.zh: 《火炬》和Politico等网站上留下的亲普京评论。

sentences.en: One of her assignments had been to write an essay from the point of view of an average American woman.
sentences.zh: 她的任务之一是从一个普通美国女性的角度写一篇短文。

sentences.en: I live in such developed society so that people have practically ceased to walk on foot, she wrote.
sentences.zh: “我生活在一个如此发达的社会中，以至于人们实际上已经停止步行了，”她写道。

sentences.en: When I emailed Aistova, she wasn't eager to talk.
sentences.zh: 当我给艾斯托娃发电子邮件时，她并不急于交谈。

sentences.en: She told me she had been harassed by critics of the Internet Research Agency after her email appeared in the leak.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，自从她的电子邮件出现在泄密事件中后，她一直受到互联网研究局批评者的骚扰。

sentences.en: Some men had even come to her door.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一些男人来到了她的家门口。

sentences.en: She would meet me for an interview, but only if she could bring her brother for protection.
sentences.zh: 她会见我进行采访，但前提是她可以带上她的兄弟以保证安全。

sentences.en: I agreed, and we met at an out-of-the-way
sentences.zh: 我同意了，我们在一个偏僻的

sentences.en: Chinese restaurant.
sentences.zh: 中餐馆见面了。

sentences.en: Aistova and her brother made an unusual pair.
sentences.zh: 艾斯托娃和她的哥哥是一对很不寻常的组合。

sentences.en: She was a short young woman with mid-length brown hair, dressed all in black, sweater, leggings, big wedge boots.
sentences.zh: 她是一个个子不高、留着中长棕发的年轻女性，一身黑衣，穿着毛衣、紧身裤和厚底靴。

sentences.en: She insisted on paying for my coffee.
sentences.zh: 她坚持要请我喝咖啡。

sentences.en: You are a Russian guest, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，你是一位俄罗斯客人。

sentences.en: He, by contrast, was a hulking skinhead with arms full of Nazi-themed tattoos, most prominent among them a five-inch swastika on his left biceps.
sentences.zh: 与她相反，他是一个身材魁梧的光头党人，双臂布满了纳粹主题的纹身，其中最显眼的是他左二头肌上一个五英寸长的卐字标志。

sentences.en: My brother, he looks like a strong man, Aistova said, giggling.
sentences.zh: 艾斯托娃咯咯笑着说，我哥哥看起来像个强壮的男人。

sentences.en: He wore a black t-shirt emblazoned with the skull and crossbones insignia of the SS Totenkopf Division, which administered the Nazi concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件黑色T恤，上面印有党卫军骷髅师的骷髅和交叉骨标志，该师曾管理过纳粹集中营。

sentences.en: I asked him what his t-shirt meant.
sentences.zh: 我问他他的T恤是什么意思。

sentences.en: Totenkopf, he grunted.
sentences.zh: 他哼了一声说，骷髅。

sentences.en: During the interview, he sat across the table from Aistova and me, smiling silently behind his sunglasses.
sentences.zh: 在采访过程中，他坐在我和艾斯托娃对面的桌子旁，墨镜后隐约带着微笑，一言不发。

sentences.en: Aistova said that she worked for the Internet Research Agency for a month and a half.
sentences.zh: 艾斯托娃说她在互联网研究局工作了一个半月。

sentences.en: The majority of her work was translating news articles from English to Russian.
sentences.zh: 她的大部分工作是将新闻文章从英语翻译成俄语。

sentences.en: The news articles covered everything from Ukraine to traffic accidents.
sentences.zh: 这些新闻文章涵盖了从乌克兰到交通事故的方方面面。

sentences.en: On a few occasions, her bosses asked her to leave comments on American news sites about Russia, but she said that they never told her what to say.
sentences.zh: 有几次，她的老板让她在美国新闻网站上发表关于俄罗斯的评论，但她说他们从未告诉她该说些什么。

sentences.en: She loves Russia, she told me.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我说，她热爱俄罗斯。

sentences.en: She truly believes that Putin is just trying to help the people of eastern Ukraine, and that his actions are being unfairly spun by the western media.
sentences.zh: 她坚信普京只是在试图帮助乌克兰东部的人民，而他的行动正被西方媒体进行不公正的歪曲。

sentences.en: I was like, hey you guys, you were saying these bad things about Putin, but people are suffering.
sentences.zh: 我当时就像是，嘿，伙计们，你们一直在对普京说这些坏话，但人们正在受苦。

sentences.en: But she claims to harbor no ill will toward the United States.
sentences.zh: 但她声称对美国没有抱持任何恶意。

sentences.en: She wants to visit New York City, she said, and see the locations from Breakfast at Tiffany's, one of her favorite filMs.
sentences.zh: 她说她想去纽约市看看，去看看她最喜欢的电影之一《蒂凡尼的早餐》中的拍摄地点。

sentences.en: I don't feel aggressive toward America.
sentences.zh: 我对美国没有敌意。

sentences.en: We're the same people.
sentences.zh: 我们是相同的人。

sentences.en: We just speak different languages, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说道，我们只是说不同的语言。

sentences.en: After the interview, we shook hands outside the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 采访结束后，我们在餐馆外面握了手。

sentences.en: You seem like a journalist who will tell the truth, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，你看起来像个会说实话的记者。

sentences.en: I wish you luck on your story.
sentences.zh: 我祝你的报道一切顺利。

sentences.en: On my last morning in St. Petersburg,
sentences.zh: 在我呆在圣彼得堡的最后一个早晨，

sentences.en: I returned to 55 Savushkina.
sentences.zh: 我回到了萨武什金娜街55号。

sentences.en: The clouds had lifted after a miserable week of snow and howling wind.
sentences.zh: 经过了一个星期糟糕的降雪和呼啸的狂风之后，云层终于散开了。

sentences.en: At a few minutes before 10, my translator and I positioned ourselves on the sidewalk in front of the entrance, hoping to catch some of the trolls as they began the day shift.
sentences.zh: 快到10点时，我和我的翻译站在入口前的人行道上，希望能趁水军们开始早班时抓到一些人。

sentences.en: This was not a very well thought out strategy.
sentences.zh: 这个策略并不是很周全。

sentences.en: Any employees arriving so close to the start of their shift didn't have time to talk to a journalist, even if they wanted to.
sentences.zh: 任何在离上班时间这么近的时候到达的员工，根本没有时间跟记者说话，即使他们愿意。

sentences.en: A large van lurched to a halt in front of us and deposited a half dozen young people who hurried in the door before we had a chance to approach them.
sentences.zh: 一辆大货车在我们面前猛地停下，放下了半打年轻人，他们在我们有机会接近他们之前就匆忙冲进了大门。

sentences.en: A bus stopped halfway down the block, and another gaggle of workers emerged.
sentences.zh: 一辆公共汽车在街区中间停了下来，又涌出了一群工人。

sentences.en: They waved off my translator's inquiries with annoyed grunts or stone-faced silence.
sentences.zh: 他们用恼怒的哼声或面无表情的沉默挥手打发了我翻译的询问。

sentences.en: A young man smoking a cigarette said he didn't work inside the building.
sentences.zh: 一个抽着烟的年轻人说他不在大楼里面工作。

sentences.en: He finished his cigarette and promptly went inside the building.
sentences.zh: 他抽完烟，随即走进了大楼。

sentences.en: At 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 上午10点

sentences.en: sharp, the flow of workers stopped.
sentences.zh: 整，工人们的人流停了下来。

sentences.en: I decided we might as well try walking inside.
sentences.zh: 我决定我们不妨也尝试走进去。

sentences.en: I had read of other journalists who tried to enter the building, only to be kicked out immediately.
sentences.zh: 我曾读到过其他记者试图进入该大楼却被立刻赶出去的报道。

sentences.en: So I entered with some trepidation.
sentences.zh: 所以我带着一些忐忑不安的心情走了进去。

sentences.en: Two men in suits guarded the turnstiles.
sentences.zh: 两个穿着西装的男人守卫着旋转闸门。

sentences.en: My translator and I approached a receptionist behind a desk and asked if we could speak with someone from Internet Research.
sentences.zh: 我和我的翻译走近前台的一位接待员，询问是否能和互联网研究公司的人谈谈。

sentences.en: It dropped the agency on moving to 55 Savushkina.
sentences.zh: 它在搬到萨武什金娜街55号时放弃了机构的称呼。

sentences.en: She informed us that Internet Research was no longer a tenant.
sentences.zh: 她告知我们，互联网研究公司已经不再是租户了。

sentences.en: A couple of months ago, we had to say goodbye because it was giving the entire building a bad reputation, she said matter-of-factly.
sentences.zh: 她语气平静地说，几个月前，我们不得不说再见，因为它给整栋大楼带来了坏名声。

sentences.en: She pointed to a board that displayed a makeshift directory of the building's current occupants.
sentences.zh: 她指着一块板子，上面展示着大楼当前住户的临时名录。

sentences.en: The names were printed out on small scraps of paper, and none of them were Internet Research.
sentences.zh: 名字是用一小张一小张的纸打印出来的，其中没有一个属于互联网研究公司。

sentences.en: But I did recognize one.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认出一个。

sentences.en: FAN, or Federal News Agency.
sentences.zh: FAN，即联邦新闻局。

sentences.en: I had read some news articles claiming that FAN was part of a network of pro-Kremlin news sites run out of 55 Savushkina, also funded by Evgenia Prigozhin.
sentences.zh: 我曾读过一些新闻报道，称FAN是萨武什金娜街55号运营的一个亲克里姆林宫新闻网站网络的一部分，同样由叶夫根尼·普里戈津资助。

sentences.en: Former Internet Research Agency employees I had spoken to said they believed FAN was another wing of the same operation, under a different name.
sentences.zh: 我曾交谈过的互联网研究局前员工表示，他们相信FAN是同一运作的另一个分支，只是换了个名字。

sentences.en: I asked to speak to someone from FAN.
sentences.zh: 我要求与FAN的人谈谈。

sentences.en: To my surprise, the receptionist picked up the phone, spoke into it for a few
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，接待员拿起电话，对着话筒说了几

sentences.en: seconds, and then informed us that Evgenia Zubarov, the editor-in-chief of FAN, would be right out to meet us.
sentences.zh: 秒钟，然后通知我们，FAN的主编叶夫根尼·祖巴罗夫马上就会出来见我们。

sentences.en: Zubarov, who looked to be in his fifties, had close-cropped salt-and-pepper hair and a weary face.
sentences.zh: 祖巴罗夫看起来五十多岁，留着剪得很短的花白头发，面容疲惫。

sentences.en: He greeted me with a handshake and invited me into his office.
sentences.zh: 他与我握手问候，并邀请我进他的办公室。

sentences.en: We made our way through the turnstiles and signed in with the guards, then took a brief walk down a long hallway to FAN's two-room office on the first floor.
sentences.zh: 我们穿过旋转闸门，在警卫那里做了登记，然后沿着长长的走廊简短地走了一段，来到了位于一楼的FAN的两室办公室。

sentences.en: It was unusually quiet for an online news operation that, according to Zubarov, had a staff of 40 people.
sentences.zh: 对于一个据祖巴罗夫所说拥有40名员工的网络新闻机构来说，这里异常安静。

sentences.en: The newsroom was equipped for a sizable team with about a dozen identical black desktop computers sitting on identical brown laminate desks.
sentences.zh: 这个新闻编辑室配备了一个相当大的团队，大约十几台一模一样的黑色台式电脑摆放在一模一样的棕色层压办公桌上。

sentences.en: But only two young reporters sat at them.
sentences.zh: 但只有两名年轻记者坐在那里。

sentences.en: The shades were drawn and the furniture looked just barely unpacked.
sentences.zh: 百叶窗拉着，家具看起来像是刚刚才拆开包装。

sentences.en: As we sat at Zubarov's desk, I told him about the articles I'd read accusing FAN of being a Kremlin propaganda outfit.
sentences.zh: 当我们坐在祖巴罗夫的办公桌旁时，我向他讲述了我读过的指责FAN是克里姆林宫宣传机构的文章。

sentences.en: He shook his head in indignation.
sentences.zh: 他愤怒地摇了摇头。

sentences.en: He turned to his computer and brought up FAN's website, pointing to the masthead and the
sentences.zh: 他转过身看着他的计算机，调出了FAN的网站，指着报头和

sentences.en: certificate number that showed FAN was an officially registered Russian mass media organization.
sentences.zh: 显示FAN是官方注册的俄罗斯大众传媒机构的证书编号。

sentences.en: FAN is a news agency, he declared.
sentences.zh: 他宣称，FAN是一家新闻机构。

sentences.en: It had stringers and reporters in Ukraine and in many former Soviet states.
sentences.zh: 它在乌克兰和许多前苏联国家拥有特约记者和记者。

sentences.en: They did original reporting, sometimes at great personal risk.
sentences.zh: 他们进行原创报道，有时还要冒着巨大的个人风险。

sentences.en: Zubarov himself was a veteran journalist who covered the annexation of Crimea for the Russian news agency Raspolt before joining FAN.
sentences.zh: 祖巴罗夫本人是一位资深记者，在加入FAN之前，曾为俄罗斯新闻机构Raspolt报道过克里米亚的吞并。

sentences.en: But ever since reports linked him to the Internet Research Agency, he had faced questions about his integrity.
sentences.zh: 但自从有报道将他与互联网研究局联系起来后，他就一直面临着对其诚信的质疑。

sentences.en: We understand being in this building may discredit us, but we can't afford to move at the moment, Zubarov said with a sigh.
sentences.zh: 祖巴罗夫叹了口气说，我们理解身处这栋大楼可能会让我们名誉扫地，但我们目前无力搬迁。

sentences.en: So we have to face the situation where reporters like you,
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不面对这样一种情况：像你这样的记者，

sentences.en: Mr. Chen, come in here and ask us questions every day.
sentences.zh: 陈先生，每天都来这里向我们提问。

sentences.en: Zubarov said he believed that he and FAN were victims of a smear campaign.
sentences.zh: 祖巴罗夫说，他相信他和FAN是一场污蔑运动的受害者。

sentences.en: I asked him who would do such a thing.
sentences.zh: 我问他是谁会做出这种事。

sentences.en: Listen, that's my position, not a confirmed fact, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，那是我的立场，而不是确凿的事实。

sentences.en: It's possible that there are some business interests, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 有可能存在某些商业利益，我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe it's an attack on our investors.
sentences.zh: 也许这是对我们投资者的攻击。

sentences.en: But when I asked who those investors were, he declined to comment.
sentences.zh: 但当我问及这些投资者是谁时，他拒绝置评。

sentences.en: I can't discuss the identities of investors, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不能讨论投资者的身份。

sentences.en: That's in my contract.
sentences.zh: 这是我的合同规定的。

sentences.en: I left St. Petersburg on April 28.
sentences.zh: 我在4月28日离开圣彼得堡。

sentences.en: One day later, FAN published an article with the headline, What does a New York Times journalist have in common with a Nazi from St. Petersburg?
sentences.zh: 一天后，FAN发表了一篇文章，标题是《纽约时报记者与圣彼得堡纳粹分子有什么共同点？》

sentences.en: The story detailed a mysterious meeting in St.
sentences.zh: 这篇报道详细描述了一场在圣

sentences.en: Petersburg between a New York Times journalist, me, and a neo-Nazi.
sentences.zh: 彼得堡发生的神秘会面，对象是一位《纽约时报》记者（也就是我）和一个新纳粹分子。

sentences.en: Its lead image was a photo of a skinhead giving an enthusiastic Nazi salute.
sentences.zh: 它的头条配图是一个光头党人热情行纳粹礼的照片。

sentences.en: But it was not just any skinhead.
sentences.zh: 但这个光头党人可不是随便什么光头党人。

sentences.en: It was the skinhead whom Katarina Aistova brought to our meeting and introduced to me as her brother.
sentences.zh: 他正是卡塔里娜·艾斯托娃带到我们的会面中并向我介绍为她哥哥的光头党人。

sentences.en: As I learned from reading the article, Aistova's brother was in fact a notorious neo-Nazi named Alexei Maximov.
sentences.zh: 正如我从阅读这篇文章中了解到的，艾斯托娃的哥哥实际上是一个名叫阿列克谢·马克西莫夫的臭名昭著的新纳粹分子。

sentences.en: The article explained that Maximov, who goes by the nickname Fly, is a member of Totenkopf, a prominent skinhead group in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 文章解释说，马克西莫夫（绰号“苍蝇”）是圣彼得堡一个著名的光头党组织“骷髅”的成员。

sentences.en: He reportedly served nine years in prison for stabbing a man to death.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他因刺死一名男子而在监狱服刑了九年。

sentences.en: Just a month before I met him, Maximov again made headlines when, during an investigation into beatings of immigrants around St. Petersburg, the police found weaponry and
sentences.zh: 就在我见他之前的一个月，马克西莫夫再次登上头条，当时在对圣彼得堡周围殴打移民事件的调查中，警方在他的公寓里发现了武器和

sentences.en: Nazi paraphernalia in his apartment.
sentences.zh: 纳粹纪念品。

sentences.en: The story made no mention of Katarina Aistova or the Internet research agency.
sentences.zh: 这篇报道没有提卡塔里娜·艾斯托娃或互联网研究局半句。

sentences.en: Instead, the article claimed I met with Maximov because I wanted his help in creating a provocation against Russia.
sentences.zh: 相反，文章声称我与马克西莫夫会面是因为我想要他的帮助来制造针对俄罗斯的挑衅。

sentences.en: Maximov told FAN that I requested to meet him because I was very keenly interested in sentiment among Russian nationalists.
sentences.zh: 马克西莫夫告诉FAN，我请求与他见面，因为我对俄罗斯民族主义者的情绪非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: He continued, he evidently needed stories about how the murderous Kremlin regime persecutes free Russian people.
sentences.zh: 他接着说，他显然需要关于谋杀成性的克里姆林宫政权如何迫害自由的俄罗斯人民的故事。

sentences.en: It's not the first time I've come across such requests on the part of Western journalists, but I'm not going to help them with this.
sentences.zh: 这不是我第一次遇到西方记者提出这种要求，但我不会在这方面帮助他们。

sentences.en: Many want to see in Russian nationalists a fifth column, which will function on orders from the West and sweep away the
sentences.zh: 许多人希望在俄罗斯民族主义者身上看到一支第五纵队，他们将在西方的命令下运作并横扫

sentences.en: Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫。

sentences.en: Apparently, I was trying to foment a mini Euromaidan right there in St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 显然，我当时正试图在圣彼得堡煽动一场微型欧洲广场革命。

sentences.en: The article was illustrated with photos of my meeting with Aistova and Maximov.
sentences.zh: 文章配发了我和艾斯托娃及马克西莫夫会面的照片。

sentences.en: One photo appears to have been shot surreptitiously through the restaurant window while we sat and talked.
sentences.zh: 其中一张照片似乎是在我们坐着交谈时通过餐馆窗户偷偷拍摄的。

sentences.en: The point of view is such that
sentences.zh: 拍摄角度使得

sentences.en: Aistova is barely visible.
sentences.zh: 艾斯托娃几乎看不见。

sentences.en: Indeed, at first glance, I seem to be having a friendly chat with a skinhead over a cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 确实，乍一看，我似乎正和一个光头党人喝着咖啡愉快地聊天。

sentences.en: Another photo, this one taken outside the restaurant, somehow makes me look deep in conversation with Maximov, even though I distinctly recall that Aistova was standing between us.
sentences.zh: 另一张照片是在餐馆外面拍摄的，不知何故让我看起来正与马克西莫夫进行深切交谈，尽管我清楚地记得艾斯托娃当时就站在我们中间。

sentences.en: I had to admire the brazenness of the scheme.
sentences.zh: 我不得不佩服这个阴谋的厚颜无耻。

sentences.en: I remembered how, at the restaurant, Aistova had sat next to me so I had to twist around to talk to her, while Maximov sat silently across from us.
sentences.zh: 我记起在餐馆里，艾斯托娃曾坐在我旁边，以至于我不得不转过身去和她说话，而马克西莫夫则一言不发地坐在我们对面。

sentences.en: Apparently, they had arranged themselves so it could appear, from the right perspective, that I was meeting
sentences.zh: 显然，他们把自己安排成那个位置，以便从正确的角度来看，可以制造出我正在与

sentences.en: Maximov alone.
sentences.zh: 马克西莫夫单独会面的假象。

sentences.en: I emailed Aistova to ask her to explain what happened.
sentences.zh: 我给艾斯托娃发了封电子邮件，请她解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: She responded only, I would also like you to explain yourself and the situation.
sentences.zh: 她仅仅回复道：我也希望你解释一下你自己和这种情况。

sentences.en: A few weeks later, when I tried calling her by phone, she pretended I had the wrong number.
sentences.zh: 几周后，当我试图给她打电话时，她假装我打错了电话。

sentences.en: Over the course of a few days, the sensational stories circulated among a network of small pro-Kremlin blogs.
sentences.zh: 在几天的时间里，这些轰动性的故事在一些小型亲克里姆林宫博客的网络中流传开来。

sentences.en: In fact, the FAN story itself had been aggregated from another pro-Kremlin news site called People's News, which Andrei Soshnikov, the Moiraion journalist,

sentences.en: As it spread, it mutated to become even more alarming.
sentences.zh: 随着它的传播，它甚至演变得更加骇人听闻。

sentences.en: One website suggested I was working for the CIA.
sentences.zh: 一个网站暗示我在为美国中情局工作。

sentences.en: Another, the National Security Agency.
sentences.zh: 另一个则暗示是国家安全局。

sentences.en: A YouTube channel called Russia Today, not the well-known state television channel, but a knockoff, posted a slick video about the meeting, set to a pounding dubstep soundtrack.
sentences.zh: 一个名为“今日俄罗斯”（不是那个著名的国家电视台频道，而是一个山寨版）的YouTube频道发布了一段制作精良的关于这次会面的视频，配上了强劲的电子重低音配乐。

sentences.en: Disconcertingly, it included a photo of me leaving my hotel.
sentences.zh: 令人不安的是，其中包含了一张我离开酒店的照片。

sentences.en: The video currently has more than 60,000 views.
sentences.zh: 这段视频目前的观看次数已超过6万次。

sentences.en: Many of those views were a result of a familiar pattern of social media promotion.
sentences.zh: 其中许多观看量是社交媒体推广的熟悉模式的结果。

sentences.en: Dozens of trolls on Twitter began tweeting links to the video using the hashtag VerbovkaNazistov, recruitment of Nazis.
sentences.zh: 推特上的几十名水军开始发推文附上该视频的链接，并使用话题标签“招募纳粹”（VerbovkaNazistov）。

sentences.en: The hashtag trended on Russian Twitter.
sentences.zh: 这个话题标签上了俄罗斯推特的热门趋势。

sentences.en: After recovering from the initial shock, I began to track the campaign against me.
sentences.zh: 在从最初的震惊中恢复过来后，我开始追踪针对我的这场运动。

sentences.en: I had practice, after all, from my months spent on the trail of the Internet Research Agency.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我在追踪互联网研究局的几个月里已经有了经验。

sentences.en: A few days later, Soshnikov chatted with me on Skype.
sentences.zh: 几天后，索什尼科夫在Skype上与我聊天。

sentences.en: Did you see an article about you on FAN?
sentences.zh: 你在FAN上看到关于你的文章了吗？

sentences.en: He asked.
sentences.zh: 他问。

sentences.en: They know you are going to publish a loud article, so they are trying to make you look stupid in front of the Russian audience.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你要发表一篇轰动的文章，所以他们正试图让你在俄罗斯受众面前显得很愚蠢。

sentences.en: I explained the setup, and as I did, I began to feel a nagging paranoia.
sentences.zh: 我解释了整个设局，正当我解释时，我开始感到一种挥之不去的偏执。

sentences.en: The more I explained, the more absurd my own words seemed.
sentences.zh: 我解释得越多，我自己的话听起来就越荒谬。

sentences.en: The more they seemed like exactly the sort of elaborate alibi a CIA agent might concoct once his cover was blown.
sentences.zh: 它们越发像是中情局特工在掩护身份败露后精心编造的那种详尽的不在场证明。

sentences.en: The trolls had done the only thing they knew how to do.
sentences.zh: 水军们做了他们唯一知道该怎么做的事。

sentences.en: But this time, they had done it well.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，他们干得很好。

sentences.en: They had gotten into my head.
sentences.zh: 他们钻进了我的脑子里。
